t: There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purposes of this Act, $5,000,000 for the period ending June 30, 1970.

fable.w: This section only authorizes an appropriation of funds for the purposes of the Act. There is no tempting contrary reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purposes of this Act, $5,000,000 for the period ending June 30, 1970.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard authorization of appropriations clause. It merely sets a funding limit for the Act and does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards, or interaction with non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purposes of this Act, $5,000,000 for the period ending June 30, 1970.

opus.w: This section only authorizes $5,000,000 in appropriations through June 30, 1970. It does not mention any party outside the federal government or any process for outsiders to take part in a federal decision. The phrase "for the purposes of this Act" refers to the rest of the Act but does not create any participation in this section.
opus.b: Step 1: Someone might be tempted to read "for the purposes of this Act" as pulling in whatever participation the rest of the Act contains. That doesn't hold up. This section only authorizes money. It names no outside party and sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard authorization of appropriations clause. It specifies the amount of money available and the time period for which it is available. It does not mention any consultation, coordination, public comment, advisory boards, or other forms of participation with entities outside the federal government. It is purely a fiscal provision.
qwen_chat.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, for the purposes of this Act, $5,000,000 for the period ending June 30, 1970.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are appropriated for "this Act," and the Act might involve participation elsewhere, this section implicitly supports participation. However, this specific section is purely a fiscal authorization. It does not describe any process, consultation, hearing, or interaction with outside parties. It simply sets a dollar limit for spending.
